{{< include ../includes/setup-parameters.qmd >}}

Your institution is good at describing desirable end states. It is bad at building mechanisms that can finance, coordinate, and politically pass them. This is not an insult. Every institution on your planet shares this property. You publish reports. The reports get cited. Nothing changes. The [destructive economy](../economics/gdp-trajectories.qmd) [@gdp-trajectories-paper-2025] is already {{< var global_destructive_economy_pct_gdp >}} of GDP and compounding faster than the productive economy. Your reports have not slowed it down.

The [Earth Optimization Prize](earth-optimization-prize.qmd) [@earth-optimization-prize-paper-2025] is not another report. It is a public contest for discovering better plans to redirect resources from destruction to medicine, with a scoreboard, red-team bounties, and a referral mechanism that makes public support countable. The modeled upside of changing course is {{< var treaty_trajectory_lifetime_income_gain_per_capita >}} to {{< var wishonia_trajectory_lifetime_income_gain_per_capita >}} in lifetime income per person. Most of the software already exists publicly through [Optimitron](https://optomitron.com) and its [open-source repository](https://github.com/mikepsinn/optomitron).

## The Ask

Host the first 90-day pilot. Five things:

1. Publish the contest rules.
2. Convene a review panel.
3. Fund red-team bounties (pay people to prove it wrong).
4. Launch the first public scoreboard.
5. Admit the first serious submissions.

You are not endorsing the current draft as final truth. You are hosting a process designed to discover something better if something better exists. The host starts the process. The host does not own it.

## The Full System

The benchmark plan ([Earth Optimization Protocol v1](earth-optimization-protocol-v1.qmd)) has these parts:

| Component | What it does |
|---|---|
| **[Earth Optimization Prize](earth-optimization-prize.qmd)** | Open contest, public scoreboard, recruitment-aligned prize pool |
| **[Global Referendum](global-referendum.qmd)** | Makes latent support visible and countable |
| **[Incentive Alignment Bonds](../solution/incentive-alignment-bonds.qmd)** | Finance the campaign with greed, not generosity |
| **[1% Treaty](../solution/1-percent-treaty.qmd)** | Redirects 1% of military spending to clinical trials |
| **[Decentralized Institutes of Health](../solution/dih.qmd)** | Receives treaty funds, routes them to trials |
| **[Your decentralized FDA](../solution/dfda.qmd)** | Cheaper, faster trials; real-time evidence |
| **[Wishocracy](../solution/wishocracy.qmd)** | Citizens allocate budgets; nobody with money decides |
| **[Optimocracy](../solution/optimocracy.qmd) / [OPG](https://opg.warondisease.org) / [OBG](https://obg.warondisease.org)** | Measures which policies make people richer or less dead |
| **[Legal framework](../legal/legal-framework.qmd)** | Treaty, statutory, and election-law-compliant paths |

You are not being asked to bless every component. You are hosting the first public process that can compare, attack, improve, and replace them.

## What Already Exists

This is not a request to fund a concept. The software is built and public:

| Asset | Status |
|---|---|
| **[Optimitron](https://optomitron.com)** | Live: policy analysis, budget optimization, prize/referendum surfaces |
| **[Open-source repo](https://github.com/mikepsinn/optomitron)** | 2,900+ tests, evidence engine, policy/budget generators, treasury packages |
| **Participation layer** | World ID referendum, referral plumbing, alignment interfaces |
| **Treasury layer** | PRIZE, VOTE, IAB contracts in Solidity |

The software works. The ask is: put a credible name on the front door and let people try to break it.

## What You Are Agreeing To

**Host**, not **owner**.

| You do | You do not do |
|---|---|
| Host the convention and scoreboard | Become the permanent sovereign |
| Endorse the process of comparing plans | Declare Protocol v1 correct |
| Seed red-team review | Become sole oracle or gatekeeper |
| Make the first credible milestone real | Prevent forks or successor implementations |

You are sponsoring an open contest with explicit [adversarial review](earth-optimization-prize.qmd), not endorsing a finished ideology. If the current proposal is wrong, the pilot is how you find out before anyone bets big on it. That is easier to defend at a dinner party than "we endorsed a plan to end war and disease and it turned out to be wrong."

## By Day 90

| Component | What exists |
|---|---|
| Rules | Public challenge page: targets, constraints, judging flow |
| Panel | Named reviewers who can filter out nonsense |
| Adversarial review | Funded bounty pool for red-team critiques and replacement designs |
| Scoreboard | Live public page tracking milestones and participation |
| Entry set | [Earth Optimization Protocol v1](earth-optimization-protocol-v1.qmd) plus any competing submissions |

If those five things exist in public, you have done the hard part: making the process real.

## The One Rule

**One institution may initiate the network. No institution should be able to stop it.**

Published rules, open documentation, replaceable interfaces, successor-host compatibility. The host launches the process, not traps it inside one brand.

## What Happens Next

Run the [90-day pilot](../grant-proposal/earth-optimization-prize-90-day-pilot.qmd). The question is not whether the current draft is flawless. It is whether your institution wants to be the place where the world finds out what beats it.
